title: Indie developers, want to test each other’s projects?
author: fwackedbubbed
selftext:
I’m hoping to find a few developers who are open to testing each other’s projects and giving honest feedback.

I’m working on a small AI multiplayer RPG, and at this stage, even a few minutes of feedback can be incredibly helpful. I’d especially like to know where the experience feels enjoyable, where it becomes confusing, and whether the AI actually makes the game more interesting.

You can comment on anything that stands out. For example:  
\-Was it easy to understand what to do?  
\-Did the AI feel responsive and consistent?  
\-Did anything feel repetitive, awkward, or broken?  
\-What would you change first?

You don’t need to write a detailed review. A quick, honest reaction is already useful.

You can try it here: [https://fictor.com/](https://fictor.com/)  
Invite code:   
ZLBAF7  
LC81BI  
6O11JP  
39B21W  
Q16GHK  
The tokens are free for now. If the invite codes run out, just send me a DM and I’ll see what I can do.

If you’re also building something, share it in the comments. I’ll gladly test it and give feedback in return. Hopefully we can help each other get closer to something people genuinely enjoy using.

I can test iOS app and website right now. If that’s what your working on, I’d be very happy to help. Hopefully we can exchange useful feedback and support each other.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body:
Right away, as I go into sort of tutorial and I can't scroll to see entire part of this tutorial or whatever it is.:

https://preview.redd.it/tbkb3x6nqplh1.png?width=3396&format=png&auto=webp&s=7ed44d8f5fbe619c94f392f661aa66f5b185b4f5

I don't have problem with other elements in the tutorial as screen moves down itself once element is entirely outside the screen. This element (3/8) didn't trigger the scroll as I suspect it didn't go over 50% of the element size?

This next thing is VERY minor and probably isn't worth bothering at all but you can see sort of square effect around dice as effect. Probably nothing, but it would drive me nuts if I was making it and I would probably spend too much time trying to fix this:

[https://imgur.com/a/0nNtpxM](https://imgur.com/a/0nNtpxM)

Also I know my dopamine receptors are fried as fuck and I might not be most focused person in the world, but some text generation was hell of hard to go through.

Also even later in the game you wait too long for generating images, in todays world people just lose focus way too fast, I get that it's a text based game, but imo it should be just... faster. Especially if you plan to have multiplayer based stories in it. Maybe a lot of pre-generated text and stuff with AI only jumping in when story went from it's course and trying to kind off steer it back towards pre-generated text. Hard to explain, but imagine game like "Wolf Among us", where you have many different options and ways to answer but story is still set on same course whatever you pick. 

So all in all my main problem was to keep focus on text and story itself. That being said I might not just be best test case for this type of game, this will require somebody who would enjoy reading a lot.

replies.author: fwackedbubbed
replies.body:
This is incredibly helpful, thank you for taking the time to go through it so thoroughly.  
The tutorial scroll issue and the dice effect border, noted. We'll get those fixed. On the text length and generation speed, you're absolutely right that it needs to be faster and more digestible, especially for multiplayer. That's something we're actively working on. Your point about pre-generated content with AI filling gaps is interesting and gives us something concrete to think about.  
Quick question: are there any games you've played where the text/narrative pacing felt right to you? Doesn't have to be AI-related, just anything where reading felt natural and didn't lose your attention. Would help us a lot as a reference point.

replies.author: fwackedbubbed
replies.body: Also, I checked out your game and honestly it blew me away. The art style is gorgeous and the whole thing feels super polished. We have a lot to learn from that.

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body:
Thanks a lot, as for your other question asked in previous message... Honestly hard to say, I didn't play much text based games, even Wolf Among Us which is heavily story driven game with mostly dialogue isn't really "text based", but my main concern would be maybe to keep focus of a player on the game, so less "long texts" and more of "here is an action" or something, maybe even add several mini puzzles that you have to solve. Even something as simple as one click:

"You come close to a door, you hear sound behind it" then Choice pops up with a door you get "Open the door" or "Walk Away" you press some of it, and then door either opens or story goes in other direction. Just small things to keep players engaged not only read text.

replies.author: fwackedbubbed
replies.body: That makes a lot of sense. Breaking up the text with small interactive moments like the door example you described is a really good way to think about it. We've been too focused on the narrative output and not enough on giving players something to do between the text. Appreciate you taking the time to explain it this way, gives us a clear direction to work on.
